items.followUp: State the first condition for equilibrium and explain what it means.

rubric.why: A body in equilibrium has neither linear nor angular acceleration; equivalently, its resultant force and resultant torque are zero.
rubric.description: Defines equilibrium by stating that both the resultant force and resultant torque are zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the zero resultant force condition and 1 mark for the zero resultant torque condition. Accept the equivalent statement that both linear and angular acceleration are zero.

rubric.why: The second condition requires the turning effects in opposite directions to balance.
rubric.description: States that the total clockwise torque equals the total anticlockwise torque.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that clockwise and anticlockwise torques or moments are equal.

rubric.why: Equal clockwise and anticlockwise torques give zero resultant torque.
rubric.description: States that the algebraic sum or net torque is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explicitly stating that the net or algebraic sum of torques is zero.

modelAnswer: A body is in equilibrium when the resultant force and resultant torque acting on it are zero.
Therefore, it has no linear acceleration and no angular acceleration.
The second condition for equilibrium is that the total clockwise torque about any point equals the total anticlockwise torque about that point.
Thus, the algebraic sum of the torques acting on the body, or the net torque, is zero.

items.followUp: Write the first equation of motion and identify the symbols used.

rubric.why: This is the second equation of motion for constant acceleration.
rubric.description: Writes the second equation of motion: s = ut + ½at².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct equation or an equivalent algebraic form.

rubric.why: This is the third equation of motion for constant acceleration.
rubric.description: Writes the third equation of motion: v² = u² + 2as.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct equation.

modelAnswer: Second equation of motion: s = ut + 1/2 at^2.
Third equation of motion: v^2 = u^2 + 2as.
